notes.content:
Happy New Year Everybody!
It's been quite sometime since I've been active on here, a lot has happened in my personal life that has affected the amount of time that I've been able to put towards development. Some of those things were wonderful, I graduated with my Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science back in May from UNC Asheville and got my first full-time position as a remote Software Engineer/Unity Developer for a small company in Asheville. But, I also lost two very close family members within months of each other and I've been left to pick up the pieces and deal with the grief that has come along with it. However, I've still managed to find chunks of time here and there to continue working on Corona. My research on CoronaAI is still in progress so the AI system is the only main ticket item remaining for the update. Rather than delaying the update even more, I have decided that I will enable Beta testing for the latest version without any AI while keeping the current 2018 Alpha version with AI live on the store. More details will be coming this week, but in the meantime, thank you for all your support throughout all these years! It's meant the world to me.
Warm regards,

notes.title: Beta 1.0.0 Nears Completion
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
It's been quite a while since I've posted anything on here. Actually, it's been about 9 months or so. The world has changed drastically, and in the darkest of times, I want to bring some joy into it. It may not be much, but maybe some good ol' Corona MotorSport could cure some of your Coronavirus blues. I've been quite busy taking a few odd jobs and various contract projects to help out my family along with juggling coursework for my third year of Computer Science, which meant that I had to put less time towards Corona (MotorSport). BUT, I'm happy to announce that the first beta is finally close to being complete. 

Some of you may be wondering why this update has taken over two years to complete, and frankly, I have the same question. To put it simply, I've had quite a hectic life during my first two years of college, and on top of that, I basically scrapped a majority of the code and assets in the current version from March 2018 and decided to rebuild the game entirely. I've reused maybe three or four scripts from the old version and had to rewrite thousands of lines of code to fix/replace deprecated features and for the sake of quality, I had to redesign a majority of the vehicles and tracks in use. Here's what's new (so far):

[h1]Beta 1.0.0 Feature List[/h1]
[list]
[*][h1]Vehicles[/h1]
[list]
[*]New vehicle - Eagle Liberator
[*]Upgraded all vehicles with new interiors and more detailed exteriors
[*]Option to change interior trim and color
[*]Complete overhaul for physics engine - switched to NWH Vehicle Physics
[*]Forced induction simulation (turbo/supercharging)
[*]New driver avatar - improved steering IK and added shifting IK
[*]New 3D tire model
[*]New Camera System
[*]Improved performance of damage system (mesh deformation will have little to no CPU overhead, damage now affects handling and engine performance)
[*]Optimized and improved vehicle sounds
[*]Improved AI - collision avoidance, faster lap times, dynamic behavior for drivers and less bugs
[/list]
[*][h1]Tracks[/h1]
[list]
[*]New track - Dubai International Circuit
[*]Redesigned Monza and Barcelona Circuits
[*]20+ additional tracks planned for release during the beta lifecycle - I'm aiming for at least one per update!
[/list]
[*][h1]Engine Specific[/h1]
[list]
[*]Updated to Unity 2019.3.0f3
[*]New Graphics pipeline overhaul - HDRP 7.2.0
[*]Improvements to NVIDIA PhysX calculations
[*]Improved framerates and performance
[*]New environment and vehicle shaders
[*]New Post-Processing stack (Improved SSR, SSAO, Color Correction, etc)
[*]UI Overhaul - Controller support, cleaner look
[/list]
[/list]

This isn't really the full list of what to expect, I'll be dropping a trailer and a update on my YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/lukejaparidze

I also want to give [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCYLiHwDmRIHEkMd7aMY0H-Q]Shinyodd[/url] and his community a special thanks for accidentally catapulting this game back into relevancy and giving me a platform to share my work and plans for the game (and a chance to redeem myself haha)! Thank you for everything!

To those of you that have been here since Corona first launched back in 2015, thank you as well! You have all helped me grow from an angsty teenager with a pet-project racing game into a young adult with the drive to succeed in this industry!

Stay safe and keep gaming!
Warm regards,

notes.title: Graphics Overhaul
notes.content:
Hey Guys!
Just another quick update on the beta build, I've decided to make the switch to Unity's new HDRP rendering system, which uses entirely new shaders and a whole new method of lighting. This should bring Corona's graphics up to par and make photorealism achievable. Massive framerate and performance improvements will also be a result of this change, as lighting will be baked into the scene data rather than calculating it each frame with a dynamic sky. Each track will feature different times and weather scenarios that are pre-rendered to choose from as opposed to just cycling through them in realtime. The old method hurt in-game performance and sacrificed render quality in exchange for constantly changing lighting and weather. I'll be posting a few screenshots as soon as I have the scenes and vehicles reconfigured for HDRP.
Cheers!
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8068925/dca660010c0ef05cd352d997fda111e6fe5b9b86.png[/img]

notes.title: Development Resumes
notes.content:
[h1]([i]This is extremely late but..[/i]) [b]Merry Christmas and Happy New Year!![/b][/h1]
Hey Guys!
Development on Corona has slowed quite a bit over the past few months, as I've been busy with my first semester of college and I'm just now starting my second semester as well. In 2012, I had a dream of starting up my own studio and publishing my creations on Steam, that dream came true in 2014, when Corona MotorSport flew through greenlight and was approved for sale. But I launched a product into Early Access that wasn't ready, and ever since then I've been working non-stop, often receiving next to nothing from sales just to finish the game. I was on the receiving end of lots of negative feedback and frankly, most of it was deserved. But I never gave up, and I don't plan on quitting anytime soon. All of you can expect Corona to be finished within a few months. I'm not finishing it because I want money, I'm finishing it because being a game developer was my childhood dream and I refuse to disappoint my current and future customers, and I hope to grow this studio and have a full team to work on projects with.

I'll keep everyone posted weekly with progress.
Stay classy and keep pushing forward, no matter how much crap life throws at you,

notes.title: Multiplayer Early Access Coming Soon!!!!
notes.content:
Hey guys!
Great news, I've officialy started working on multiplayer for the game! It's going quite well so far, I've managed to get a very basic test scene running that will autoconnect to a master server, I can drive the car I set up around with ease and with only a tad bit of jitter/lag, some more tinkering with the serialization scripts should do the trick. So, in order to anticipate what's next for the alpha version of Corona MotorSport Multiplayer, please read below.

[h1]The Multiplayer Testing Phase[/h1]
As of now, the hosting solution I am using to test multiplayer functionality is Photon Unity Networking, their free plan allows 20 concurent users (CCU), which is plenty for the first phase of testing (would probably last 3-4 weeks). During the first phase, the multiplayer will be open to anyone with a copy of the game to access, however, only 20 users (including myself) would be able to play at one time, so play sessions would be limited to approximately 30 minutes per person with unlimited reconnections. So you could play for 30 minutes, the server would automatically kick you after 30 minutes to allow others to try it out, but if there's room, you are welcome to rejoin.

So during the first 3-4 weeks of multiplayer, there would be one trackday server (choose a car, and just drive around with other people) with a limit of 20 people. After working out all the bugs, I'll upgrade to 100CCU, which would allow 5 servers with up to 20 people each. I'll keep going and adding more user capicity based on demand.

Dedicated server hosting by third parties (that's you guys!) would also be available in the future as well as LAN multiplayer and split screen multiplayer.

Thank you for your continued support!
Luke Japaridze
Shivu Sharma
LucasGame Studios
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8068925/dca660010c0ef05cd352d997fda111e6fe5b9b86.png[/img]

notes.title: Update 2.06 releasing March 13th!
notes.content:
Hey guys,
Been very busy with the latest update. So far, numerous bugfixes have been made along with some performance improvements. A full settings menu will (finally) be present with the ability to recall previously saved settings. A new, simple, lag-free menu (the showroom will still be accessible) and a full on weather system (new sky package).

This new system will improve overall game performance and increase it's visual quality. Atmospheric scattering has been implemented as well. As the weather changes, so will the qualities of the track. For example if it begins to rain, the track will become more slippery, pretty self explanitory. I hope to have racing AI included in this update, if not, I will be purchasing a different AI physics package as the one I have gotten (was present in earlier versions of the game) is very glitchy, difficult to setup properly and behaves erratically. 

We are nearing the one year anniversary (March 13th) of Corona MotorSport's initial launch on steam. It's been a great year and I can't thank you guys enough for your support, I never dreamed of getting this far and I look forward to continue developing for steam for many years to come. I can't provide an exact date as to when corona motorsport will be fully finished and transfer to a full title release but I can promise the journey will be great. As I've mentioned before, I am currently working out licensing deals with several vehicle manufacturers so I can promise many new real-world cars this year. notes.title: Graphics Upgrade!!!
notes.content:
Hey guys,
Another progress report on Update 2.05:

I've updated to Unity 5.2.1, which brought along some new features in the engine that allowed me to import and create some advanced stuff. One of those things being Screen-Space Reflections (notice the car reflections on the floor, thats SSR, reflection probes can't do that), which allows creating realistic reflections without sacrificing performance. there are some imperfections to SSR so I will use it in combination with what CMS currently uses: reflection probes. Unity 5.3 will solve issues with reflections and bring in native support for SSR and allow smoother blending between the two methods, so it may look a tad bit wierd now but it will look much better when Unity 5.3 is released.

I've also added in new custom shaders, which will work together with Unity's standard shaders. The new shaders allow me to do things like adding dynamic snow, rain, or animated illumination. Many other features have been added in and now there is full support for changing the vehicle's colors as well as having new texture designs.

I've also improved the quality of the driver character, upping the texture quality to 2k for his clothing and skin. Ive also rigged blendshapes which will allow smooth and realistic facial animations (will be useful for story mode). Im working on smooth shifting animations as well.

There's also a lot of texture improvements, added normal and specular maps on more objects and some displacement maps for tesselation (the walls in the garage have tesselation, adds some more depth ːsteamhappyː)

Anyways, here's a shot showcasing the new graphics:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/rME9OUA.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/K5Ml2Xc.png[/img]

Thank you for your continued support and we look forward to releasing Update 2.05!!!!!!
Luke Japaridze (Lead Developer)

notes.content:
Hey guys, sorry this update took so long, there was a lot of work that needed to be done on the game to make it more stable, less buggy, and have better graphics.
[h1]What's New?[/h1]
[list]
[*]New driver model - will be the protagonist of the story, nicknamed "Lazarus" (yes it's a cliché lol), also added a new IK system for realistic driver animation and steering
[*]Changed from Gamma Color Space to Linear Color Space - apparently choosing something from a dropdown menu seemed to make a huge difference in lighting
[*]Changed from DirectX 9 to DirectX 11 - Not really noticable, but should just look a little better in general and gives me more options for shader coding. The game can still run on DX9 systems, can someone confirm that for me?
[*]Fixed some reflection probes on the maps, they now appear less dull and grey and more vibrant now
[*]Telemetry System - added a whole bunch of gui that provides accurate and realtime information about the car such as torque, rpm, clutch status, fuel level, steering wheel position, current gear, and speed. Race data is also shown (current lap, checkpoint, lap time, race time)
[*]Lap system - The game now has a lap system with a race time and a lap time
[*]New Car - Trophy Truck
[*]Re-added Stunt Plane with basic island map (temporary)
[*]Re-designed Serato Conquistador - Redid the back with a glass engine cover, cleaned up some imperfections on the body.
[*]Color picker for all cars
[*]Normal Mapped tire textures for better lighting
[*]Cabin lights for all cars (linear lighting gets darker at night than Gamma lighting)
[*]Fixed headlight intensities and distances (again, linear lighting functions differently)
[*]Cinema quality Motion Blur - realistic looking motion blur added to cameras, costs about 5-10 fps depending on system (I have a 4gb GTX 960 and the game runs between 55-120 fps on max settings depending on the car and map)
[*]Basic settings menu incorporated into pause menu
[/list]
Ill be on vacation from the 12th to the 22nd in the Dominican Republic and probably will have very limited wifi or time to respond to people on the forums and wont be able to work on the game so the next update will be delayed a little. 

ps: I will patch in a settings menu in a few days for those with low-end computers to finetune graphics settings more precisely rather than just choosing from a list of preconfigured settings. Also, I have found out whats causing the excessive flickering on the cars and maps, its the Bloom effect, no matter what value its set to it always produces that flicker, Im working on a solution for it. The stuntplane is also a bit buggy, there's still issues with the wheels and the map isn't the best quality but those will be fixed shortly. Also the camera in the main menu sometimes clips through the plane because its huge compared to the cars, thats also being fixed

Anyways, enjoy the update!
